name: PT Akasha Wira International Tbk

frontmatter.title: Akasha Wira International — a quality franchise priced close to its value inside a tight float
frontmatter.summary: Akasha Wira sells bottled water, Korean-style food and salon hair care, with net cash, a bond portfolio and returns on equity in the high twenties after nearly doubling sales in two years. A ten-for-one split clears the exchange's minimum free-float share count but not the percentage gap that binds in March. DCF above the price, multiples below; HOLD, on a target the split leaves untouched.
thesis: {'Two profitable franchises, not one': "bottled water and food sit beside a cosmetics range that earns most of the group's gross profit [S2]."}
{'Growth is manufactured by distribution, not declared': 'the 2025 and first-half 2026 step came from extending reach, and both segments grew together [S3].'}
{'The cash engine funds the build': 'net cash, a bond portfolio and capex above a quarter of sales while the plants go up [S2][S3].'}

The DCF, at 60% weight, values the shares at Rp30,445 against Rp28,500 — above the price but well short of the BUY threshold, so HOLD on its own; the multiple cross-checks sit well below both, and the blend keeps the rating HOLD [S0][S2].
The controlled float, the HSC listing and the March 2027 free-float step cap any re-rating until the register changes [S8][S10][S11].

catalysts.event: Extraordinary shareholders' meeting to approve the ten-for-one stock split
Trading on the post-split nominal is expected to begin in the regular and negotiation markets
First free-float step to the intermediate threshold, or a controller sell-down to meet it
FY2026 audited accounts, on the FY2025 rhythm: those were authorised for issue on 25 March 2026
MSCI decision on the proposed move to Standalone status

blocks.text: **What changed.** On 12 November Akasha announced a ten-for-one stock split: the count rises from 589,896,800 shares to 5,898,968,000 and the nominal falls to Rp100 a share, subject to approval on 16 December 2026, with trading on the new nominal expected from 15 January 2027 [S17][S18]. The stated purpose is the exchange's minimum number of publicly held shares: the float of 47,833,459 shares was 2,166,541 short of the 50,000,000-share floor, which the split clears without a sale or an issue [S17][S18]. Management states ownership percentages and the value of a holding are unchanged [S18] — which is why it does not touch the binding constraint, the 8.1% free float that must reach 12.5% by 31 March 2027 [S10][S11]. That is the company's public-share count under the exchange rule [S17][S11]; the annual report's residual public line is a slightly wider measure [S4].

The split leaves our forecasts, valuation and rating untouched: it multiplies the share count and divides per-share value by the same factor. Every per-share figure is on the pre-split base — the last price of Rp28,500 and the target of Rp29,620 — because no archived source shows the split effective and the data pack is unadjusted [S0][S18]. What did move the target is the model work: the bond portfolio now enters the valuation, FY2026E revenue is rebased on the company's own second-half seasonality, and terminal reinvestment is set consistently with the return earned. Those changes roughly offset, and the rating stays **HOLD** at Rp29,620 against Rp28,500, a total return of 3.9%.

The variant view is not that the company is misunderstood — the market has noticed. It is that a de-rated Indonesian consumer multiple is being applied to a business that has shown it can grow far faster than the category, while the DCF values the franchise at Rp30,445 a share against the Rp28,500 price — a premium well short of the BUY threshold, so HOLD on its own [S2][S3]. At today's price the market discounts FY2027E revenue growth of 20.9% against the 22.0% we forecast, and pays 15.8x on this year's earnings [S0]: a couple of points of growth, not the existence of the franchise.

Three things move the value: whether the 2026 step is repeatable [S3]; capital intensity, since capex above a quarter of sales has to fall for the cash flow to show [S0]; and the float [S10][S11]. The konglo lens in the valuation section prices that regime; the multiple weights, not the lens, are why the target sits below the DCF.

Akasha Wira is a Jakarta consumer manufacturer with two segments. Food and beverage bottles drinking water under the Nestlé Pure Life and Vica brands, sells soy milk under Pureal and has moved into Korean-style food under Mujigae and Wonhae; cosmetics makes and sells the Makarizo salon hair-care range alongside licensed Wella and Clairol products [S2][S4].

The revenue split is close to even, and that is the single most important fact about the business. In FY2025 food and beverage produced IDR1,374.6bn of net sales and cosmetics IDR1,352.3bn out of IDR2,727.0bn [S2]. The profit split is not even: cosmetics generated IDR849.7bn of gross profit against IDR580.8bn — hair care earns a segment margin in the low sixties, bottled water one in the low forties [S2]. Water is the volume and the distribution footprint; hair care is where the money is made, and a reader who models ADES as a water company will get the margin structure wrong.

The stated objective is the average annual gain in intrinsic value per share rather than a reported profit line; the 2025 and 2026 growth came from extending distribution reach across the islands and pushing both portfolios through it [S4]. Sales are entirely to third parties [S2].

The footprint is domestic with a rounding-error export tail — water in West and East Java, food in West Java, cosmetics in Bogor — and 1,862 employees, because distribution leans on third-party logistics [S2][S4].

Control is absolute: Waters Partners Bottling SA held 91.35% at end-2025, through Sofos Pte Ltd in Singapore to Andy Pe; the entity began as a Coca-Cola and Nestle joint venture acquired by Sofos in 2008, so the brand licences are a reliance worth stating: the hair-care trademarks come from Marlene International, a third party under a 2010 agreement, not from the controlling group [S2][S4].

Bottled water in Indonesia is large, structurally growing and expanded again in 2025, but dominated by well-established players with scale and resources, so share is won on execution and distribution [S4]. ADES is a challenger in water with a national brand licence and a regional plant base. Hair care is a different fight: Makarizo sells through salons as well as retail, a professional channel mass brands do not own, which is why cosmetics earns a materially higher gross margin — at the price of dependence on the channel and the licence [S2].

Raw materials were IDR618.1bn of FY2025 cost of goods sold and packaging IDR352.9bn; resin follows the oil and palm complex, but the house agri deck's CPO path sits only a few per cent above spot and most of the move passes through [S2]. The real drivers are distribution reach, trade mix and the rupiah cost of imported inputs [S4].

Five forces: supplier power is moderate, packaging bought at scale [S2]; buyer power is high in modern trade, low in general trade; entry barriers are brand and salon relationships in hair care, low technical ones in water; substitutes cap mass-segment pricing; rivalry is intense, as the company says [S4].

The moat is distribution density [S3][S4]. Whether that is durable or a one-off land grab is the central question; for it, two years of repetition; against, incumbents defending shelf space. We treat the moat as real but narrowing after the forecast window, which is why terminal growth sits at 5.0%, below nominal GDP. Regulation is product and packaging related, none of it idiosyncratic except the brand licences [S2].

Revenue went from IDR1,291.0bn in FY2022 to IDR2,727.0bn in FY2025 — FY2024 growing 28.3%, FY2025 39.4% — while net profit more than doubled to IDR741.6bn, a net margin of 27.2% [S0][S2]. Gross margin held in the low fifties: cosmetics, up about two-thirds in two years while water grew about a fifth, offset input costs [S2].

FY2026E revenue is IDR4,663.1bn, growth of 71.0%: the first half filed at IDR2,027.2bn [S3], the pack's third quarter taking nine-month sales about three-quarters up year on year [S0], and a fourth quarter set on the company's own FY2025 seasonality, where the second half was about a third larger than the first [S3][S0]. Holding Q4 flat at the Q3 run-rate would assume that seasonal lift disappears, which nothing in the filings shows. Growth then fades to 22.0% in FY2027E and 12.0% by FY2030E: a challenger cannot compound at a share-grab rate once the shelf space is taken [S3][S4].

Margins are anchored on the printed quarters, not the FY2025 peak and not the first half alone. Gross margin is 48.1% in FY2026E against 52.5% in FY2025: the 2026 path fell in each successive quarter, with the third quarter the weakest of the three; the fourth quarter is set at that third-quarter rate because no filing discloses a price increase or an input pass-through that would reverse it [S0][S3]. The quarter-on-quarter fall is the packaging-resin and palm-derived input squeeze on the water and food lines, partly offset by the higher-margin cosmetics share [S2][S3]. The forecast then holds the 2026 exit rate flat at 48.0% through FY2030E, because a return to FY2025's 52.5% is a recovery that enters only when a quarter prints it [S0]. It is held, not recovered, to the terminal year: FY2035E is 47.6%, so the 2026 input-cost step is treated as permanent rather than as a cyclical dip that mean-reverts. Operating overhead is held at 20.0% of sales, the H1 level, because selling expenses grow with revenue [S3]. The bridge is arithmetic: 48.1% less 20.0% plus D&A of 2.6% gives an EBITDA margin of 30.7%, against 34.4% in FY2025. Tax is held at 21.5%: the reported 2026 quarters already charge around that rate, the September quarter at the top of their range, so we anchor on the 2026 run-rate rather than FY2025's lower effective rate, which flattered the base year on non-taxable interest income [S0][S3].

One restatement matters: the pack's FY2025 D&A of a few billion rupiah is a fragment against the IDR70.2bn charged in FY2025 and IDR55.9bn in FY2024 [S2]. The cash-flow statement is direct-method, so the pack never captured the real charge; we restate it and the engine rebuilds EBITDA [S2][S0]. Revenue, cost of sales and profit agree with the audited accounts [S2].

Cash conversion is the weakest part. Operating cash flow was IDR564.8bn in FY2025 against net profit of IDR741.6bn, IDR471.8bn against IDR527.4bn in FY2024 and IDR459.6bn against IDR395.8bn in FY2023 [S2][S14]; the accrual gap went from negative in FY2023 to mid single digits of average assets in FY2025, widening on the pack's twelve-month figures [S0][S14]; still below the house flag, a watch item consistent with a distribution push where receivables and inventories outgrew sales [S0][S3]. FY2026E free cash flow to the firm is IDR-559.5bn, negative, on capex of IDR1,305.7bn and the working-capital step [S0].

The balance sheet is the strongest part: basically no debt at end-2025, cash and short-term investments of IDR990.3bn, equity IDR3,000.7bn [S2], and IDR372.7bn of Indonesian government bonds as a non-current financial asset, roughly a quarter more than at end-2025 [S3]. Net debt stays negative at -0.3 times EBITDA [S0]. Cash builds to IDR3,219.3bn by FY2030E because no dividend is paid: every rupiah of profit is retained [S2][S0] — rational in a build phase, a governance point for minorities.

With a risk-free rate of 7.4% and an unlevered beta of 0.70 the beta build gives a cost of equity below the IDR band, because the beta captures market risk but not a register with 92.4% insider ownership and an 8.1% float; the disclosed 0.5% register premium takes WACC to 11.0%, the bottom of the band, and the valuation section sets out what that floor position costs the return [S0][S8].

Earnings-quality flags, through the house screen. Accruals: below the threshold but deteriorating — a watch item, and the same item seen from the balance sheet, where receivables and inventory outgrew sales. Regime: the special-board exit of September 2026 came in the reshuffle that rewrote the price, free-float and liquidity criteria — rule-driven, not a company rehabilitation, and normal auction mechanics are restored while the concentrated-ownership status is not [S7]. Related parties: the only related-party trading flow the FY2025 note discloses is IDR0.1bn of purchases from PT Roundhill Nusantara, an entity under common control; the Marlene licence is a third-party brand licence and is not counted there [S2]. Structure: no pledge, no rights issue, no serial dilution — checked, none found. The one flag is optics-class: a controlled company with a large cash balance and no dividend depends on the controller's discipline. We haircut nothing for it: the valuation credits net cash and the bond portfolio at face value because they sit in deposits and government bonds rather than an operating claim [S2][S3].

We value ADES on a discounted cash flow to the firm, weighted 60% in the house method set the industry config fixes for this template, with a P/E cross-check at 30% and EV/EBITDA at 10%. The set fits a growing, debt-free consumer manufacturer; a single year's earnings would value it mid-step at the profit level of the year before the step.

11.0% is the bottom of the house's mandated IDR cost-of-capital band, and that position is a stated choice rather than a neutral output. The beta build gives 11.0%, below the band, because a 0.70 industry beta cannot see a register with 92.4% insider ownership and a 8.1% float, so we add the smallest disclosed register premium, 0.5%, that reaches the floor. The grid below runs the DCF a point either side of that rate, so a reader who prefers the middle of the band sees that case explicitly; the risk section says what it does to the return.

The terminal is built to survive the test that matters: at 5.0% growth it is funded by reinvestment consistent with the return the explicit period earns, not by growth without capital. Struck on FY2035E EBITDA of IDR3,362.7bn, the terminal value implies an exit EV/EBITDA of eight point eight times — well below the 11.4x the market pays at entry, above the 7.9 times peer-median-and-own-history blend the cross-check uses, and a shade above the eight and three-quarter times ADES itself averaged over the four years the engine measures [S0]. The DCF therefore does not ask a buyer to pay a re-rating at exit, but its headroom against the company's own history is close to nil, and the terminal carries 66.8% of the DCF value because the terminal year still earns a return on invested capital in the low twenties against a cost of capital at the band floor. That spread is the residual optimism in the valuation: it rests on the salon channel and the distribution density lasting, and the sensitivity grid is the honest test of it — terminal growth a point lower and the discount rate a point higher each take the value down materially [S0].

The cross-checks disagree loudly: P/E yields Rp19,798 a share on 11.0 times and EV/EBITDA Rp18,283 on 7.9 times — -35.0% and -39.9% against the DCF, and well below the price [S0]. Three reasons, one about ADES: trailing earnings are a backward anchor for a company that grew revenue by more than half in six months; the benchmark averages a peer median and ADES's own four years, both collapsed after a long de-rating; and the peer set runs from four-to-six-times microcaps to ICBP and MYOR, so the median describes an illiquid small-cap, not a name with a net margin of 27.2%. The cross-checks are a floor on what a de-rated market will pay.

We keep the house weights but say which side we believe for twelve months. The DCF describes value if growth holds; the multiples describe what a buyer pays today for a name with only 8.1% of its shares in public hands. A quality-matched cross-check sits between: the market pays 15.8x on this year's earnings and, at the same Rp28,500 price, 13.3x on next year's — the shares de-rate through the growth rather than being paid for it. That is the strongest argument against the DCF, and why the target is built from the weighted, liquidity-adjusted fundamental value of Rp26,583 [S0][S2]; the gap comes from the multiple weights, not the regime overlay.

The konglo lens then sets the twelve-month price. ADES is on the high-shareholding-concentration list [S8], its float of 8.1% is below the new minimum with a step due inside the window [S10][S11], the stock is out of the IHSG calculation [S9] and MSCI has opened a consultation on Standalone status [S12]. Fundamental value today is Rp23,940 and Rp28,500 sits 1.19 times it — a premium, not a discount; the twelve-month fundamental value is Rp26,583. The regime cases are the shares of the log gap that **close**: base 40%, giving Rp29,515; bear 80%, giving Rp27,526, where a small premium still survives rather than a discount reopening; bull -5%, the premium widening as a sell-down fixes the float, giving Rp31,924 [S8][S10][S12]. The weighted target is Rp29,620; the lens changes no operating assumption, and the split is arithmetic in none of these numbers, leaving the premium, target and total return unchanged [S17][S18].

Ranked by likelihood times impact. First, **the growth step proving a pull-forward** (medium likelihood, high impact): if the push loaded the trade rather than expanded it, FY2027 undershoots the fade and the DCF's terminal collapses towards the multiple values [S3]. Second, **capital intensity** (medium, high): capex above a quarter of sales with negative free cash flow means betting on demand not yet invoiced [S0][S3]. Third, **the free-float overhang** (high, medium): the gap is 4.4% of the register; the block a sell-down needs is many multiples of the three-month traded value of IDR1,134.8m a day, so it clears only at a discount, while a placement would dilute the controller alongside minorities [S8][S10][S11]. The split answers the share-count leg, not the percentage leg that costs the controller shares [S17][S18].

Fourth, **input and packaging costs** (medium, medium): a resin or rupiah shock moves gross margin further than our links imply [S2]. Fifth, **brand-licence risk** (low, high): the hair-care trademarks are licensed from Marlene International, a third party, under the 2010 agreement, and a change in terms would hit the segment earning most of the gross profit [S2]. Sixth, **governance and liquidity** (low, medium): mechanics are normal after the special-board exit, but traded value is thin for a company this size and amplifies every flow [S7][S0]. Seventh, **the discount rate** (medium, high): our 11.0% sits at the floor of the house band, and at its midpoint — a point higher — the DCF value per share on the sensitivity grid above falls below the Rp28,500 price and the 3.9% total return turns negative. The HOLD is therefore a floor-of-band view: a mid-band rate on the same cash flows takes both the DCF and the blended value below the Rp28,500 price, and that is the case the sensitivity grid is there to show [S0][S2].

The business scenarios are mirrored on the operating drivers. In the bear, revenue growth runs four points lower in every year — a return to the category rather than a share gain — the input squeeze does not ease and the gross margin gives back a further two points; the share count also rises five per cent on a discounted primary placement, the mechanism the float deadline makes possible and the one asymmetry we allow the tails, because no equivalent buyback is plausible for a controller at 91.35%. In the bull the same two operating drivers move the other way and the float is fixed by a sell-down rather than an issue. Probabilities are 25.0% bear, 50.0% base and 25.0% bull: the base is the most likely path, and the tails symmetric rather than leaning bearish to look careful [S3][S4].

The regime path runs the other way and is not in the bear. A sell-down that takes the float to the threshold by 31 March 2027 would end the HSC listing, restore IHSG and LQ45 eligibility and remove the two regime adjustments the lens applies, with the premium allowed to widen — the bull regime case at Rp31,924 [S8][S11][S12]. We do not remove the 10.0% liquidity discount there: a sell-down raises the float, not the traded value.

Waters Partners Bottling SA holds 91.35%, the public the rest, and control runs through Singapore and Swiss holding companies to a single individual [S4]. The controller determines any vote; the exchange free-float measure of 8.1% [S0][S8] — the public-share count the rule tests [S11] — is below the exchange minimum, with an intermediate step to 12.5% by 31 March 2027 and a final step by 31 March 2028, a gap of 4.4% and 4.5 months [S10][S11]; and the stock sits on the HSC list, out of the IHSG calculation [S8][S9]. The gap must be closed by a sell-down, a new issue or a register change, with different consequences for minorities, and no filing says which route [S11].

The ten-for-one split sits apart from those three. It is mechanical: the float goes from 47,833,459 shares to a post-split count close to ten times the 50,000,000-share floor, the nominal falls to Rp100, and management states ownership percentages and the value of a holding are unchanged [S17][S18].

What ADES does not carry is enforcement — no OJK action, no special notation, no litigation disclosed in the filings we reviewed, and the special-board exit leaves the HSC status, the index exclusion and the float where they were [S4][S7].

Related-party dealings are narrow and disclosed. The FY2025 note records one related-party trading flow, purchases of IDR0.1bn from PT Roundhill Nusantara under common control [S2]. The licence line is larger — IDR64.5bn — but it is a third-party brand licence: Marlene International, licensor under the 25 October 2010 agreement, is not designated a related party in the FY2025 accounts, and the IDR21.9bn it billed in FY2025 was settled against a refundable deposit [S2 notes 11, 29a]. The agreement runs to 2030 at a percentage of cosmetics net sales, so the exposure is disclosed, long-standing and in our margin forecast — an optics-class concentration flag and a reason not to pay a premium multiple, not a channel of value leakage we can quantify or a related-party flow.

Audit and reporting are clean: an unqualified FY2025 opinion from Tanubrata Sutanto Fahmi Bambang & Partners, a mid-tier firm rather than a global network, neither improper nor irrelevant at this size [S4]. The board is led by a president director while the controller sits offshore, concentrating decision-making; the annual report's disclosures are the main minority protection.

On ESG the exposures are inherent to the category: water stewardship and sourcing, packaging waste and producer-responsibility obligations, and labour standards in a largely contract workforce of 1,862 [S4]. Targets are not disclosed; the packaging obligation has a visible cost line and sits inside our cost assumptions.

We watch a list, each chosen because a move would change the model: revenue growth by segment, because cosmetics carries most of the gross profit [S2]; gross margin against the latest quarter [S3]; capex as a share of sales, because the DCF depends on the build ending [S0]; the accrual gap and receivables and inventory days [S0][S14]; licence fees as a share of sales [S2]; and the register, including any placement or rights issue [S11]. After the split we add traded value in rupiah as the liquidity test [S18].

The signposts that would make us wrong are specific: if the second half of 2026 shows revenue reverting to the pre-2026 trajectory, the fade is too generous and the multiple cross-checks, not the DCF, are the right value; if capex stays at a quarter of sales into FY2028E, free cash flow never arrives; and if the float is fixed by issuing new shares, per-share value falls for a reason that has nothing to do with the business [S10][S11]. We would move to BUY if the price fell far enough below the blended fundamental value to clear the threshold without the operating evidence improving [S2]..

bear.narrative: The distribution step proves partly borrowed: competing water and hair-care brands defend shelf space, the 2026 bulge turns out to have pulled forward some trade stock, and group growth runs four points below base in every year, so the long-run growth input falls to 1% - no real growth, a return to the category rather than a share gain - and FY2027E grows in the high teens only because the second half of 2026 is already invoiced; the mix stays in water, the food margin does not recover, and the gross margin gives back 2pp. The share count also rises 5% on a primary placement priced at a discount to fund a float the controller would otherwise have to sell. This matches the mirrored shock on the operating drivers, the same amounts the bull adds, so the tails stay symmetric; the placement is the one asymmetry and it is the downside mechanism the report describes, not a second opinion on the business.

bull.narrative: The share gains hold: the extended distribution keeps compounding and the cosmetics range takes national salon and modern-trade share, so growth runs 4pp above base with a gross margin 2pp higher as premium mix builds; the register also fixes itself, because a secondary sell-down takes the float to the March 2027 threshold without issuing a share, which is the path the regime lens prices as its own bull case.

12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

adjustments.why: on the exchange's HSC list (as of 2026-10-22): out of the IHSG, the LQ45/IDX30/IDX80 and the MSCI indexes [konglo deck S3]
free float 8.11% must reach 12.5% by 2027-03-31 — controller sell-down or new shares inside the window [konglo deck S25]

konglo.construction: target = fundamental 12-month value (probability-weighted business scenarios, after the liquidity discount) x the probability-weighted share of today's premium kept, (price / fundamental value today)^(1 - c) over the regime scenarios; c = share of the log gap that closes within 12 months

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E 71.0% is the nine-month actual plus a fourth quarter on the company's own FY2025 second-half/first-half seasonality: H1 2026 revenue was Rp2,027.2bn (F19, S3) and FY2025's second half was 1.30x its first half (FY2025 revenue Rp2,727.0bn less H1 2025 revenue of Rp1,186.2bn, the base F19 implies, leaves H2 2025 at Rp1,540.8bn), so H2 2026 at the same ratio is about Rp2,635bn and FY2026E about Rp4,662bn. That is not a forecast step - it is what the filed first half and the data pack's third quarter (Rp1,214.4bn, S0, about 75% up on the same nine months of 2025) already show, with food and beverage +78% and cosmetics +64% in H1 (F22, F23). Holding Q4 flat at the Q3 run-rate would put H2 at 1.20x H1 and would assume the seasonal fourth-quarter lift disappears, which nothing in the filings shows. FY2027E 22% then fades the step: the group is doubling off a Rp2.7trn base in a bottled-water market that grows at single digits, so the share-gain phase cannot compound at 60% once distribution has been extended. FY2028E 17%, FY2029E 14%, FY2030E 12%, long run 5% (below Indonesian nominal GDP growth of roughly 8.5%, the ceiling a mature water and hair-care franchise should hold).

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Anchored on the latest printed quarter, not the first half. Nine-month 2026 gross profit is Rp1,580.9bn on Rp3,241.6bn of sales (H1 gross profit Rp1,017.0bn on Rp2,027.2bn, F20; Q3 gross profit Rp563.9bn on Rp1,214.4bn, S0), a 48.8% nine-month margin. Q4 is set at the Q3 rate, giving a 48.1% FY2026E group margin: the quarterly path is 51.9% / 48.6% / 46.4% and there is no sourced evidence - no price increase, no input pass-through disclosed - of the reversal that a first-half anchor would require in the fourth quarter. The whole forecast then holds the 2026 exit rate flat. FY2025 was 52.5% (F5, F3); the roughly 4pp fall through 2026 is the packaging-resin and palm-derived input squeeze plus the mix shift towards the lower-margin water and food lines at a 47.6% cosmetics revenue share (F18, F17, F22, F23). The model does not assume that squeeze reverses: it reverses only when a printed quarter shows it, and until then the forecast carries the evidenced level rather than the FY2025 peak. The 2026 step is therefore treated as permanent within the forecast horizon: the margin is held at the 2026 exit rate and ends at 47.6% in FY2035E, not back at the 52.5% FY2025 peak.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: 12% of COGS, derived from the input breakdown rather than asserted. Packaging and indirect materials were 27.2% of FY2025 COGS (F25, S2 note 22). Bottling and hair-care packaging is mostly PET and HDPE, whose resin price is set by the oil and palm-derived monomer complex; taking resin at roughly 40% of packaging cost (the remainder is labels, cartons, closures and third-party conversion) gives about 11% of COGS, to which the palm-derived fatty alcohols and surfactants in the Makarizo formulations add approximately 1% (inside raw materials, 47.7% of COGS, F24). The resin share of packaging is a judgment, not a disclosed line; it is disclosed here so a reader can re-run it. At three times this link (36% of COGS) and 65% pass-through, a CPO path 5% above spot moves FY2027E gross margin by about a point (the engine run at 0.36 gives 49.4% against 50.4% at 0.12); the exposure matters in a palm spike, not in the base case.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: 65%. A 4% exposure is small enough to pass through over a year: management lifted the marketing spend and repriced the range through 2025 while gross margin held above 50% (F20), so the pricing channel exists. Not 100% because bottled water is a price-led, high-velocity category where list prices move slowly.

assumptions.label: Cost link 2: share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: 2% of COGS. Link 2 is wheat (d.agri.wheat), which reaches ADES only through the food range - the soy-milk and Mujigae Korean food lines launched in 2021 - and those sit inside the food and beverage segment's Rp1,374.6bn of sales (F15). Water bottling, the bulk of that segment, has no wheat content.

assumptions.label: Cost link 2: pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: 70%. The food range is a small, newer portfolio sold at premium Korean-food positioning, where repricing is easier than in bottled water; but the category is competitive and the brand is young, so we do not assume full pass-through.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: 20.0%, the H1 2026 actual (selling Rp362.9bn plus G&A Rp42.1bn on Rp2,027.2bn of sales, F21). FY2025 was 20.7% (unallocated expenses Rp563.7bn, S2 note 31). Held flat: the company is adding distribution and marketing as fast as sales, so there is no operating-leverage assumption beyond the licence fee (2.4% of sales, F26) being fixed.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2026E 2.6% is the FY2025 charge of Rp70.2bn (F1) over sales, restated from the LK note 10 because the data pack carried only Rp9.3bn. It rises to 3.4% by FY2030E as the current capacity build (Rp386.6bn of capex in FY2025, F13, and a further step-up in 2026) enters service on 8-15 year machinery lives (S2 note 2l).

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2026E 28%, the last twelve months' actual: capex was Rp1,152bn on LTM sales of Rp4,120bn (S0, the sum of the four quarters, of which Rp772.6bn fell in the single third quarter of 2026 as PPE rose from Rp1,190bn at end-2025 to Rp2,162bn at 30 September 2026), and the filed first half was Rp206.1bn (S3, cash flow). 28% of FY2026E sales is about Rp1,305bn, which is the Rp978.8bn spent in the nine months plus a fourth quarter at about the first-half quarterly rate and well below the third-quarter lump: the step-down from the third quarter is the build completing, not a forecast of less building than the company has already done. It then fades to 20% (FY2027E), 15%, 11% and 9% (FY2030E) as the plants come into service, and to 8.5% in the long run. That long-run rate is not maintenance alone: it is D&A of 3.4% plus the net investment a 5% grower needs at the return the balance sheet earns, because reinvesting (5% / 25%) of NOPAT, or about 5.1% of sales at these margins, is what keeps the terminal growth and the terminal return consistent with the explicit period.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: 20.8% of sales, on one definition throughout: the finance-side definition the engine carries, current assets excluding cash less current liabilities, which was Rp567.3bn on Rp2,727bn of FY2025 revenue (S0). That definition includes prepayments and other current liabilities on both sides of the net, so it is broader than the trade components alone - receivables Rp468.1bn plus inventories Rp400.8bn less payables Rp263.6bn is Rp605.3bn, or 22.2% of sales (S2) - and the two are not mixed. The broader definition is used because it is what the engine's balance sheet reconciles to; 20.8% is its measured FY2025 level. It is a distribution-heavy balance sheet with trade credit to modern-trade customers and stock in the water and cosmetics chains, so the ratio does not fall as the company grows.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: 21.5%, anchored on the 2026 run-rate rather than on FY2025. The three reported 2026 quarters charge at 21.2%, 21.0% and 21.5% (Q1-Q3, S0), so the nine-month effective rate is above the FY2025 20.9% (tax Rp195.6bn on pre-tax Rp937.2bn, S2 note 31) and the latest quarter prints the rate we forecast. The FY2025 gap to the 22% statutory rate came from non-taxable interest income; since the 2026 charges are higher, we do not carry that benefit forward. A rate at the top of the 2026 quarterly range is the most likely path and is not a conservatism: it is the last actual.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: 8.5%. The company was debt-free at end-2025 (finance expense Rp0.1bn, F10); the Rp127.5bn of borrowings at 30 September 2026 (S0) is new and small, so we price it at the Indonesian corporate rate rather than at the meaningless historical average.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: 5.0%. Finance income of Rp51.6bn on a Rp990bn cash balance plus debt instruments (F9) implies roughly 5%; the policy rate in the house macro deck is 5.75%, so 5% is the right forward yield on a liquidity portfolio.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Zero. The company funds the build from operating cash and its Rp1trn cash pile; the small Q3 2026 drawdown is treated as working-capital timing, not a funding plan, and no source shows a debt-funded capex programme.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Zero. Other income net was Rp18.9bn in FY2025 (S2 note 31) - mostly FX gains, unrealised gains on short-term investments and asset-sale gains - which is not a recurring operating item and should not be capitalised into the forecast.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Zero. The company has no minority interest on its balance sheet or in its profit (S2): all subsidiaries are wholly owned.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: 0%. No dividend has been declared or paid in the four years we hold (S0 dividend history) and the FY2025 statement of changes in equity shows retained earnings rising by the full profit with no distribution (F11). The controlling shareholder's stated objective is to maximise intrinsic value per share and the company is in a capacity build, so retention is the most likely policy; we do not assume a payout that has never been paid.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Zero. 589,896,800 shares at end-2025, unchanged all year (F14), and no rights issue or placement is disclosed. The ten-for-one split announced on 12 November 2026 changes the number of shares and the nominal value but not ownership percentages or the value of a holding (F40-F42, S17, S18), so it is not a change in the economic share count we model; the per-share outputs stay on the pre-split base until the 15 January 2027 effective date (S18). The percentage free-float remedy may still be met by the controller selling down rather than by issuing shares; a new issue would be a dilution event and is treated as a risk, not a base case.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: 5.0%. Below the 8.5% long-run nominal GDP growth implied by the house deck (real 5.29% plus CPI 3.28%), appropriate for a mature bottled-water and hair-care franchise whose categories grow with population and per-capita spend rather than with GDP-plus.

challenges.challenge: The report says the DCF credits the liquidity portfolio at face value (section 3, section 4: 'it sits in bank deposits and short-term debt instruments'), but fund record market.investments = 0.0, bridge_items = [], and the DCF bridge is only Q3 cash 703.654 less debt 127.475 = -576.179. S2 p.4 shows Rp297.271bn of non-current 'Investments in debt instruments' at end-2025, separate from cash 935.624 + ST placement 10.000 + ST investments 44.695. If the portfolio is still held at 30 Sep 2026 it is omitted; Rp297.271bn over 589.8968m shares (F43) is about Rp500/share, enough on the model's 32,174 target and 29,325 price to cross the 10% ADD band and break the HOLD. If it was sold, the report must say so and reconcile the Q3 cash.
challenges.answer: The debt-instrument portfolio is now in the model, not just the prose: F44 takes Rp372.702bn at 30 June 2026 from the S3 balance sheet and note 12 total row, the same face value as the Rp297.271bn at end-2025 that S2 p.4 shows, and valuation.bridge carries it at probability 1.0. Every method credits it (the multiples' bridge becomes -948.881 from cash 703.654 less debt 127.475 less the portfolio), and the rating is re-run: HOLD, target 31,768 against a price of 29,325, a total return of 8.3%. Section 3 and section 4 now say the portfolio is bridged separately from the pack's cash because the two do not overlap.

challenges.challenge: Section 4 says the base regime case 'keeps 40% of the log gap', the bear 'keeps 80%', and 'the discount reopens'; the engine's compress.base 0.4 / bear 0.8 are the shares of the log gap that CLOSE (fund record qc prints 'the base case closes 40%'), and the bear's premium_kept is 1.006235, a 0.6% premium, not a discount. The report's own reproducibility claim fails: keeping 40% of the 3.16% premium gives a different number from the printed 32,160.
challenges.answer: The prose now states the compress values as the shares of the log gap that close in twelve months, as fund record qc prints them: base closes 40% and gives 31,737, bear closes 80% and gives 30,932, bull closes minus 5% and gives 32,667, with premium kept of 1.039, 1.013 and 1.070 respectively. The claim that the discount reopens is deleted; the bear leaves a small premium because 1.0663 to the power 0.2 is above one. The bull case is the premium widening as a sell-down fixes the float.

challenges.challenge: Section 4 calls the trailing multiples 'a floor on what a de-rated market will pay, not a valuation', but gives them 40% of the method set; the DCF alone is 39,161 (+33.5%, BUY) and the 60/30/10 weights produce 31,566 (+7.6%) and the 32,174 target (+9.7%), 0.3pp below ADD. No house standard or source pins 60/30/10; the weight is a judgment that decides the rating.
challenges.answer: The 60/30/10 set is the house standard, not an analyst choice: operating configuration fixes FOOD_BEVERAGE at dcf_fcff 0.6, pe 0.3, ev_ebitda 0.1 with multiple_source blend. We tested the alternatives the review asked for: 70/20/10 gives 32,482 and 10.8% (ADD), 80/10/10 gives 32,862 and 12.1% (ADD), 100% DCF gives 33,548 and 14.4% (ADD), and the house 60/30/10 gives 31,768 and 8.3% (HOLD). The rating therefore turns on the house weight, which is disclosed in section 4 with the DCF's own value of 36,900, and we do not override the config to reach a preferred label.

challenges.challenge: Terminal value is 66.2% of the DCF at g = 5.0% (the house cap, no fade below), and the implied exit EV/EBITDA is not printed; the report tests it only against the entry 11.4x, not the peer median 7.06x or own history 8.75x. The terminal ROIC implied by 5% growth and the capex/D&A step is far above the explicit-period ~25% ROIIC, so the terminal is not moat-justified in the card's sense; the multiple-survival test is incomplete.
challenges.answer: Terminal reinvestment is now ROIC-consistent rather than growth without capital: capex at the long end is 8.5% of sales = D&A of 3.4% (F1, S2) plus 5.1% of growth capital, which funds terminal growth at approximately the 25% return the explicit period earns out of the coefficient g/ROIC x NOPAT. The prior 5.5% left a terminal return several times the explicit-period figure and is withdrawn. The exit multiple that results sits below the market's entry multiple of 11.0x and above the peer median of 7.06x and ADES's own four-year 8.75x; the report states that gap as the residual optimism and carries terminal growth at the house cap instead of fading it, because a fade below the cap would be an unsourced haircut.

challenges.challenge: FY2026E revenue 4,458.6 is 9M 3,241.5 plus Q4 at the Q3 run-rate 1,214.4; the assumptions file gives no source for holding Q4 flat, and FY2025 H2/H1 was about 1.3x (S3/F3). If Q4 follows last year's seasonality, FY2026E revenue and the DCF are higher and the 9.7% return may cross ADD. This is a default conservatism, not the company's plan.
challenges.answer: Q4 2026 is now set on the company's own seasonality rather than a flat run-rate: FY2025's second half was 1.30x the first (S3, F3), so H1 2026 revenue of Rp2,027.2bn scales to FY2026E revenue of Rp4,663bn, growth of 71.0%, about Rp204bn above the flat-Q4 build. The value effect is partly offset by the capex and terminal-reinvestment corrections in C4 and C6, and the target moves from 32,174 to 31,768. Section 3 says why holding Q4 flat would assume the seasonal lift disappears, which no filing shows.

challenges.challenge: The assumptions file says LTM capex was 1,152 (28% of LTM sales) but uses 25% for FY2026E with no source for the 3pp step-down; the qc justification calls it 'construction that is already in the ground and finishing' without a capex plan or guidance. At the LTM 28% on FY2026E sales 4,458.6, capex would be about 130bn higher and FCFF lower; the base is optimistic on the largest cash-flow swing.
challenges.answer: FY2026E capex is now the 28% of sales the last twelve months already printed, not a 25% step-down: LTM capex Rp1,152bn on LTM sales Rp4,120bn, with PPE up from Rp1,190bn at end-2025 to Rp2,162bn at 30 September 2026 in the pack's Q3 balance sheet, against H1 filed capex of Rp206.1bn and the Q3 lump of Rp772.6bn. Capex is therefore Rp1,306bn in FY2026E and free cash flow to the firm is negative, as section 3 now shows. The long-run 8.5% is the ROIC-consistent maintenance plus growth figure described in C4.

challenges.challenge: The bull is only the mirrored business shock; it omits the register path the report itself describes: a controller sell-down or placement lifting the free float to 12.5% by 31 Mar 2027 (S11), exit from the HSC list and restoration of IHSG/LQ45/MSCI eligibility (S8/S9/S12), which would compress the small-float premium the 10% liquidity discount and 11.0% WACC assume. The 2027 MSCI decision avoiding Standalone is a second re-rating path. The float is treated only as an overhang.
challenges.answer: The register path is now in the report rather than only in the risks list: section 5 states that a sell-down taking the float to the threshold by 31 March 2027 would end the HSC listing, restore IHSG and LQ45 eligibility and remove the two regime adjustments, giving the bull regime case of 32,667, and that we do not remove the 10% liquidity discount there because a sell-down raises the float, not the traded value. The business bull stays the mirrored operating shock at 43,242 so that the regime and operating cases are not double-counted in the scenario probabilities.

challenges.challenge: The base holds the long-run gross margin at 52.0% (the FY2025 level) 'not above it' and the bull adds only 1.5pp, but the segment data show the margin-accretive cosmetics business at 62.8% (F18) against food and beverage at 42.3% (F17); a faster mix shift could exceed the 52% cap. The report gives no evidence 52% is the structural ceiling, so the cap reads as a default haircut rather than a sourced most-likely path.
challenges.answer: The long-run gross margin is 47.6% by FY2035E, not the FY2025 52.5% peak: the model holds the FY2026 exit rate (48.1% group, anchored on the printed Q3) flat and carries it to the terminal year, treating the packaging-resin and palm-derived input squeeze and the mix shift towards water and food as permanent until a printed quarter shows reversal. The 2026 give-back is the filed quarterly path, not a default haircut; the bull adds 2pp for premium mix, and the segment arithmetic (cosmetics 62.8%, food and beverage 42.3%) still reproduces the group figure. The ceiling is the evidenced level, not a cap below the actual [S2][S3].

challenges.challenge: The bear is the mirrored -3pp growth / -1.5pp margin shock; it omits the placement/sell-down supply event the report itself quantifies in section 5: a ~5% issue at a ~20% discount costs ~1% per share (the report's number), and a controller sell-down to meet the 12.5% step into an ADTV of 1.1bn is a block-trade overhang. A rights issue or discounted placement would change the per-share arithmetic, which the report says is the risk but does not put in the scenarios.
challenges.answer: The placement is now a bear shock, not only a risk paragraph: the bear raises the share count by five per cent on a discounted primary placement, the mechanism the 31 March 2027 free-float step makes possible, alongside revenue growth four points lower and gross margin two points lower. It is the one asymmetry we allow the tails and it is justified in qc_justifications scenario.mirror: no equivalent buyback is plausible for a controller above ninety per cent, so forcing one into the bull would invent a transaction no filing or regulation requires.

challenges.challenge: The bear's -3pp growth still leaves FY2027E growth at about 19%, a huge share gain, and the narrative says the 2026 bulge may have pulled forward trade stock, but no shock captures a reversion to the single-digit category growth the report itself cites. The bear is a mild slowdown, not the plausible downside; the report should show a scenario where growth returns to the category and the margin gives back the mix gain.
challenges.answer: The bear growth shock is widened from three points to four points below base in every year, on top of the two-point margin give-back, so it compounds to a substantially lower FY2030E revenue rather than a mild slowdown, and the bear target is 26,060, eleven per cent below the price. A one-year reversion to category growth is also named in section 7 as the signpost that would make the multiple cross-checks, not the DCF, the right value; we keep the multi-year -4pp path as the most likely downside because the filings show the step still running in the third quarter of 2026.

challenges.challenge: Section 3 calls the whole Rp64.482bn licence line 'a real related-party flow ... about a fortieth of sales', and section 6 says it is 'largely under the 2010 agreement with Marlene International'; F26 says only Rp21.9bn was billed by Marlene, and the related-party note 32 quote names only PT Roundhill (F27). The related-party share is therefore about 0.8% of sales, not 2.4%, and the 'controlling network' characterization is not in the archived quote. The earnings-quality gate's related-party percentage is overstated threefold.
challenges.answer: The related-party share of the licence line is corrected to the Marlene-billed amount: F45 takes Rp21.878bn from note 11 of the FY2025 accounts, which is 0.8% of sales, against the total licence expense of Rp64.482bn in F26, so the rest is paid to third-party brand owners. Section 3 and section 6 now say the related-party part is well under one per cent of sales, and the characterisation of the controlling network is removed because no archived quote supports it. The screen's related-party percentage is now the 0.8%, not a fortieth of sales.

challenges.challenge: The house card requires valuation.post_bs_review; fund record has none, and the prior review's FIX Q2 was left open at sign-off. The 12 Nov split announcement and the 30 Sep 2026 Q3 balance sheet are exactly the post-balance-sheet events it should cover; the split is value-neutral but the Q3 cash and investments are not.
challenges.answer: valuation.post_bs_review is now in fund record with four sources: the 12 November split announcement, which is value-neutral and leaves the register where it was; the 30 September 2026 pack, whose cash of Rp703.7bn sits apart from the debt-instrument portfolio; the H1 net additions of about Rp68.4bn to that portfolio; and no other material event found between the balance-sheet dates and the asof date. The prior FIX Q2 is closed by this entry.

challenges.challenge: Thesis bullet 4 says 'the DCF's ADD'; the DCF is 39,161 vs the 29,325 price, +33.5%, which is BUY under the limits (>=25%), not ADD. The final HOLD comes from the 40% multiple weight, not from the DCF; the label misstates the model's own rating.
challenges.answer: The thesis bullet now says the DCF at 0.6 weight stands at 30,445 against the 28,500 price — a premium of about 7%, well short of the 25% BUY threshold, so the DCF alone is HOLD, not BUY. The P/E and EV/EBITDA values sit about 35% and 40% below the DCF and carry the other 40% of the house weights, so the blend also lands HOLD. The pre-revision 36,900 and 29,325 figures cited in the original challenge are superseded by the terminal-reinvestment fix; the current engine run is the basis of this answer [S0].

challenges.challenge: The catalyst table dates the FY2026 audited results 2027-03-31 to S3, the 2027-06-30 AGM to S4, and the 2027-04-30 MSCI feedback close to S12; S3 is the H1 2026 filing, S4 the FY2025 annual report, and S12 says only 'by the end of June 2027' plus an interim update, with no April date. The dates may be right but the cited sources do not say them.
challenges.answer: The catalyst dates now carry the sources that state them: the 16 December 2026 meeting and the 15 January 2027 trading start from the split announcement [S18], the 31 March 2027 float step from the exchange rule [S11], the FY2026 audited accounts at the four-month statutory limit, end-April 2027 [S17], and the MSCI decision by the end of June 2027 [S12]. The April feedback window and the June AGM rows are deleted because no registered source states those dates.

challenges.challenge: The 8.11% free float is cited to [S8][S10][S13]; the prior review's FIX Q1 found S13 does not name ADES or 8.11% (it is the general 956-issuer free-float article), and the registry/deck S25 is the source. F37/F43 give the count, so the percentage is arithmetic. The FIX was outstanding at the prior sign-off and is still open.
challenges.answer: The float is no longer cited to S13. The percentage is shown as the data pack's market block and the exchange's concentrated-ownership list [S0][S8], and the count leg is arithmetic from F37, F38 and F39 in the split paragraph: the shares held publicly were short of the floor and the ten-for-one split clears it. The prior FIX Q1 is closed by the changed citation.

challenges.challenge: The update is 6,914 words against the 3,500-word cap (lint WARN); the split is explained in the summary, section 3, section 4 (two paragraphs), section 5, section 6 and section 7, and section 6 repeats auditor/ESG material. The required new information (the split mechanics and the pre/post-split base) is a fraction of that.
challenges.answer: The report is now 3,499 words, inside the 500-3,500 range for an update, down from 6,914. The split is explained once in the summary and once under governance, the duplicated governance prose and auditor material are merged, and the section 4 and section 5 overlap is cut without dropping any required section: business, industry, financials, valuation, risks and scenarios, governance and ESG, catalysts.

challenges.challenge: The summary says 'Nothing in our forecasts, our valuation or our rating changes', but the published v1 target was 32,140 (queue status) and the current model target is 32,174; the split is value-neutral, so the 34 difference is from other model updates (Q3 pack/registry/price date) and is not reconciled. A reader is told nothing changed while the target moved.
challenges.answer: The summary no longer says nothing changed. It says the split leaves forecasts, valuation and rating untouched, and then names what did move the target: the debt-instrument portfolio entering the valuation, FY2026E revenue rebased on the company's own second-half seasonality, and terminal reinvestment set consistently with the return earned. Those changes take the published 32,140 to 31,768 and they roughly offset, which is why the rating stays HOLD.

challenges.challenge: Investment summary paragraph 3 and thesis bullet 4 still call the engine DCF of Rp30,445 a BUY on its own. Against the Rp28,500 last price that is about +6.8 percent, inside the HOLD band under the +25 percent BUY hurdle, so the sentence overstates the primary method. The recorded C13 answer also still cites the pre-revision 36,900.
challenges.answer: Investment summary and thesis bullet 4 now state the DCF standing: 30,445 against the 28,500 price, above it but well short of the 25% BUY threshold, so the DCF alone is HOLD; the blend keeps the rating HOLD. The C13 rationale is refreshed to the current engine DCF, superseding 36,900 [S0].

challenges.challenge: Section 4 still says the P/E and EV/EBITDA cross-checks are both under half the DCF, but Rp19,798 and Rp18,283 are about 65 percent and 60 percent of Rp30,445. The same paragraph says 15.8x on next years earnings lands close to today price; on the model FY2027E EPS of Rp2,139 that is about Rp33,800, some 19 percent above the Rp28,500 price and above the engine DCF, which inverts the argument it is used for.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now gives the cross-checks through engine placeholders as -35.0% and -39.9% against the DCF, well below rather than under half, and drops the close-to-price claim: at the same price the multiple is 15.8x this year and 13.3x next, so the shares de-rate through the growth [S0].

challenges.challenge: The 2027-04-30 catalyst still cites S2 and says FY2025 was filed on the same rhythm, but S2 shows the FY2025 accounts were authorised for issue on 25 March 2026, five weeks before the four-month limit, and states no filing deadline.
challenges.answer: The FY2026 catalyst is now dated 2027-03-25 on the FY2025 rhythm, citing the 25 March 2026 authorisation for issue in S2; the unsourced four-month-limit and 30 April claims are removed rather than patched [S2].

challenges.challenge: QC NOTE Q5 is unaddressed: the long-run gross margin falls to 47.6 percent by FY2035E and never recovers toward the FY2025 52.5 percent, while the recorded C8 answer still says the long run reaches about 52.0 percent effective.
challenges.answer: The gross-margin basis now states the 2026 input-cost step is treated as permanent in the forecast horizon and ends at 47.6% in FY2035E, not the FY2025 52.5% peak; the C8 answer is refreshed to describe the 47.6% model instead of the stale 52.0% [S2][S3].

challenges.challenge: QC NOTE Q6 is unaddressed: the report uses an 8.11 percent free float and an 8.65 percent public holding without saying which definition it uses, and the Q6 comparison figures (premium 1.22x, cases 30,024/27,684/32,894) no longer match the current engine (premium 1.19x, cases 29,515/27,526/31,924).
challenges.answer: The report now names the 8.1% as the company's public-share count under the exchange rule (S17/S11), distinct from the annual report's residual public line (S4/S8). Sign-off figures are engine placeholders from the current run: premium 1.19x and regime cases 29,515/27,526/31,924; the QC note's 1.22x and 30,024/27,684/32,894 predate the price refresh [S0][S17].

missing_bull_case.note: The business bull is the mirrored +3pp growth / +1.5pp margin; missing are the register re-rating path (float to 12.5% by 31 Mar 2027, HSC exit, IHSG/index re-inclusion, MSCI Standalone avoided) and a faster cosmetics mix (F18 62.8% vs F17 42.3%) beyond the 52% base cap. The float is treated only as an overhang.

missing_bear_case.note: The bear is only the mirrored -3pp / -1.5pp shock and still assumes high-teens FY2027 growth; it omits the placement/sell-down supply event the report itself quantifies in section 5, a trade-stock pull-forward/reversion to single-digit category growth, and the MSCI Standalone outcome. The joint downside is described but not in the scenario set.

assumption_realism.note: Q4 FY2026 is held at the Q3 run-rate with no source (FY2025 H2/H1 about 1.3x, S3/F3); capex is 25% of sales against the LTM 28% cited in the same file; gross margin 50.5% base vs 50.2% H1 actual; terminal g at the 5.0% cap with no fade and no terminal ROIC test. Growth and opex are consistent with the filings.

evidence_and_citations.note: Split dates (S18) and H1/9M figures (S3/S0) verify. But the licence is called a related-party flow at the full 64.482 when F26 says only 21.9 was billed by Marlene; the 8.11% float cites S13 (prior FIX Q1; S13 does not name ADES); the FY2026-results, AGM and April-2027 MSCI catalyst dates cite S3/S4/S12, none of which state them.
